event: On St. Brigid's second-floor hall, Nimue fills a coffee cup, six minutes left on her shift.
She has mapped the hall without meaning to: two exits, the crash cart, the drunk in 210.
Even off the clock she counts the room: who's breathing, what's between her and the door.
Flat blue-white text hangs in the air before her: THE SYSTEM HAS DESCENDED.
Coffee overflows the cup and scalds her fingers; she leaves them there.
The System: 99.4% fail the threshold for Ascension; culling completes in 00:60:00.
A countdown starts in the corner of her eye, and she cannot blink it off.
Down the hall Devon laughs, then drops mid-step without putting his hands out.
Nimue is over him at once: no pulse, no breath, no wound, pupils blown and fixed.
She starts compressions anyway, elbows locked, counting.
Soft thuds sound through the whole hospital and the whole city as people drop.
A footnote: resuscitation will not restore an unascended subject; nothing to repair.
Nimue does six more compressions, then stops, because the System is right.
She stands, knees wet with spilled coffee, as the clock reads 00:57:12.
Priya from peds seizes her wrist and begs her to say what to do.
Nimue reaches in herself for warm reassurance and finds it is not there.
She grips Priya in a transport hold and orders her to the south stairwell, away from windows.
Priya looks at her like she was handed a rock, then goes.
Eleven seconds later the sky comes down, without a sound.
Through the east window the city folds inward along seams that were not there before.
Up through the seam rises the Tower, a dark fluted column scored with rings.
Nimue counts about a hundred rings and cannot be sure even of that.
The Tower's shadow falls the wrong way, toward the brightening east.
The shadow crosses St. Brigid's: the lights, the call bells and the coffee machine die.
Gravity tilts toward the Tower, and a low hum settles in her teeth and bones.
The air smells of ozone, and of a city with its power off.
At 00:54:40 Nimue has her back to the wall by the crash cart, still counting.
A child screams in room 218.
In 218, three patients lie dead; a boy of about nine with a cast sits up, alive.
The window is gone, a clean seam in the air, and something has come through it.
It is greyhound-sized, all joints and wet grey hide, a cluster of System light for a face.
It turns, slow, toward the loudest soft thing in the room: the boy.
A System box names it: Threshold Warden, a Tier 0 scout that hunts by sound, fragile and fast.
Nimue snags on fragile and sees the flaw: the light-cluster is its eyes.
She crosses the room and covers the boy's head with her body: through me first.
Her right hand tears the IV pole off its wheeled base.
As the warden launches, she drives the pole's point into its reading face.
The warden shrieks and dissolves around the pole; the boy cries into her scrubs.
The System: Floor Spawn neutralized; subject engaged a Tier 0 hostile prior to Ascension.
Nimue understands the System is scoring her: every reflex is data toward her worth.
At 00:49:03 she crouches and asks the boy his name: Marcus.
She sends Marcus to Priya in the south stairwell, and does not tell him it will be okay.
Marcus runs.
At 00:48:51 Nimue weighs the pole and turns toward the seam and the Tower.
She walks into the city: streets intact, traffic dead, everything leaning toward the Tower.
The other 0.6% are on the streets too.
A man slumped over a bus wheel thins away like fog off glass, leaving ozone.
A dead woman on a bench comes apart; her oranges roll into the gutter.
All over the city the System tidies the dead away, on schedule.
A knot of survivors huddles round a parked car; System text blooms over their heads.
Nimue does not stop: engage, or be cleared.
She does not look back, and lets her survivor's guilt push her on.
A dozen others converge on the Tower's base, none of them talking.
Halfway there the System posts: one hundred floors stand between the ascended and the apex.
Each trial yields essence; her designation is HARVESTER. The Tower keeps what you cannot.
She sets harvester aside with everything she can't use yet, and keeps walking.
She recalls her mother: Nimue is a drowned-legend name, the lady who masters the tower.
She lets the legend go: work clears floors.
At the Tower's base the threshold is a seam in the world, edged in blue-white.
Others reach their own seams along the base, each alone; the clock reads 00:11:46.
Nimue steps up to the line and sets down the pole's foot; the seam does not open.
The System asks for an anchor: when the System fell, what did you reach for?
Option A, Last Stand: her body made a wall for the child; +3 VIT.
Option B, Killing Edge: the pole torn loose and driven home; +2 PWR, +1 SPD.
Option C, Open Eye: the reach for the interface itself; +2 ATT, +1 INS.
Three versions of one instant in room 218 take shape in the blue-white air.
Behind her the last of the unascended thin into ozone, and the dead city goes quiet.
Nimue stands on the line, and the seam waits to be told what to make of her.
